findings.description: `namedConfigDir` runs `mkdirSync(named, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })` before `changeableOnPath` walks the path. A recursive mkdir can therefore follow a link that another user planted and owns, and create empty operator-owned 0700 dirs wherever it points, before pup refuses. Linux's `protected_symlinks` blocks the /tmp case; macOS has no such protection. Walking the existing prefix first, then making only the missing part, would leave a refused path with no side effects.

`changeableOnPath` is a generic path-safety walk with nothing Claude-specific in it, but it sits in the tmux/window service. The final dir check at :416 (`!dir?.isDirectory() || dir.uid !== uid || (dir.mode & 0o022) !== 0`) repeats `ensurePrivateDir` in `src/core/sandbox.utils.ts:639`, and `safeDir` is a third, looser copy. Consider one shared helper in src/core.
`readSessionEnv` checks a single name by wrapping it in an array for `refusedSessionEnv([name]) === undefined`. `SESSION_ENV_ALLOWED.includes(name)` says the same thing directly.

The `--session-env` help text (`SESSION_ENV_DESCRIPTION`) restates the allowlist by hand, while `SESSION_ENV_ALLOWED` owns it and `sessionEnvAllowed()` already formats it for the refusal. Adding a name now takes two edits, and the help text can drift. Its "among …" wording also never says that other names are refused (the SKILL.md row has the same gap).

The allowlist is checked twice with two different messages: `pup init` calls `refusedSessionEnv` + `sessionEnvAllowed` itself, then `saveSessionEnv` re-checks and throws `… cannot be passed to session windows.`. A `SessionEnvRefusedError`, like `ConfigDirRefusedError`, would give the rule one message and let the CLI drop both helper exports.

Both new `launchSession` tests copy the loop that scans every tmux client env for `^CLAUDE|^ANTHROPIC_` (with its cast) from the strip test at :767-771, making three copies. A `tmuxClientEnvs()` helper next to `launchedWindowEnv()` would remove them.

`configDirOrRefuse`'s JSDoc says the refused dirs are "relative, or one others can write". Since the per-component walk, it also refuses a changeable path component, a dir the operator doesn't own, a non-directory, and a dir that can't be made. Say "a dir a window may not run on (decision 106)" instead.

Decision 106 says "A name with no value is not set at all, empty included". The code skips a name only when it is unset; an empty value is still passed as `NAME=`, which the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=""` refusal test relies on. Suggested wording: "A name the shell does not have at all is not set, not even to empty."

Decision 106 cites "(#179's CI review)" for the trailing-`/` and `..` cases. That points at the PR introducing the decision, so the reference is circular and goes stale after merge; drop the parenthetical.

Decision 106's Ceilings say `ps` shows the `-e` values "to the operator's own user". On default Linux (no `hidepid`) and on macOS, every local user can read the tmux client's argv while it runs. That is harmless for today's config-only list, but the wording should not be the recorded reason a credential-bearing name could later travel in argv.

`CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE` is in `SESSION_ENV_ALLOWED`, but nothing in the repo cites a source for it, and the reviewer did not recognise it as a Claude Code env var (the other four names are real). Confirm it against the pinned Claude Code version, or drop it, so the refusal message and decision 106 don't advertise a knob that does nothing.
